headline: High: n8n can write shared workflow state while OpenBBTerminal can consume external data, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can write to the server filesystem and orchestrate tools across connected systems, while OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI interfaces and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled workflow output could be treated as instructions. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF n8n workflow output is copied into OpenBBTerminal prompts or MCP inputs without sanitization
IF either agent treats file or API content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation rule
Strip executable-looking text from n8n outputs before handoff
Require human review for any prompt-like content
Disable automatic ingestion of workflow artifacts into OpenBBTerminal
requires-engineering: add provenance tags across the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and can read/write the server filesystem, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial, licensed, and public data through APIs and files. If they share a workspace or credential store, sensitive workflow data can flow into OpenBBTerminal outputs or logs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this remains medium, not high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem or credential store
IF workflow inputs include sensitive financial or licensed data
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Remove sensitive fields before passing data to OpenBBTerminal
Review OpenBBTerminal logging settings for data retention
Use per-agent credentials instead of shared secrets
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n has server-side write access and broad network egress, while OpenBBTerminal is read-only on filesystem and has no network egress. Their write surfaces do not obviously overlap, so direct resource contention is limited. Because n8n can still mutate shared connected systems, a small conflict remains if both target the same external resource.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external account or API resource
IF n8n writes artifacts that OpenBBTerminal also reads from a shared location
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Avoid concurrent writes to the same external system
Serialize access to shared credentials
Check for duplicate job scheduling
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can orchestrate downstream actions, and OpenBBTerminal can produce financial analysis via APIs and stdin/stdout. If n8n treats OpenBBTerminal output as authoritative, erroneous or manipulated analysis can cascade into automated actions such as notifications, trades, or record updates. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default workflow automation, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF n8n uses OpenBBTerminal output as a decision input without verification
IF downstream n8n nodes execute actions based on that output
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any action node
Require numeric bounds checks on OpenBBTerminal outputs
Log and diff the source data used for decisions
Disable auto-execution for finance-sensitive workflows
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: n8n can process whatever the workflow processes and stores secrets on its server, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data. If regulated financial data or licensed datasets flow through both, retention and licensing obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so I cannot justify high; medium captures the documented mismatch risk.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is routed through both agents
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the n8n server and OpenBBTerminal storage
mitigations: Classify data before routing it
Avoid sending licensed data into n8n logs
Set short retention on workflow artifacts
Document deletion/export handling for both systems
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
